title: Cardinal Labs POC: Quality Evaluation Plan and Benchmarks
summary: POC scoping focused on a 6-week pilot to validate quality for Cardinal Labs' customer-facing summarization feature. Agreed on golden prompts, regression test sets, hallucination and format checks, scoring rubric and sample sizes. Next steps: Redwood to share eval harness, sample scoring spreadsheet, and initial pricing for Dedicated pilot. Customer to produce 2k anonymized ground-truth pairs and identify 8 golden prompts.
next_steps: Redwood: Send eval harness link and scoring template by 2025-04-04
Cardinal: Upload 2k anonymized reference summaries by 2025-04-10
Schedule follow-up run-through of harness w/ SE and Eng on 2025-04-11
action_items: Olivia Park: Prepare initial eval harness repo and README (due 2025-04-04)
Maya Rodriguez: Confirm golden prompt list and edge-case examples (due 2025-04-09)
Trevor Liu: Provision S3 bucket and share creds for sample upload (due 2025-04-08)
Samir Patel: Send draft pricing/commit options for Dedicated pilot (due 2025-04-06)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~64 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Olivia (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood Solutions), Maya (Cardinal Head of ML), Trevor (Platform Eng), Nina (PM), Ethan (Data Eng)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um quick intros? We'll keep this focused on the POC scoping and quality eval plan.
[00:15] Maya: Hi all, Maya here, thanks. We're most concerned about accuracy for our summarization UI — customers will notice hallucinations and broken formats very quickly.
[00:30] Olivia: Totally, and we want to make sure we set concrete success criteria and a defensible scoring approach. I have a proposed rubric to walk through.
[00:45] Trevor: Quick note, from infra side we care about throughput at peak and also how long evaluation runs take, because CI is nightly.
[01:10] Samir: Great point Trevor; we'll separate the quality eval from the runtime perf benchmarks but capture both for the POC.
[01:30] Diego: I'll flag that for Dedicated sizing if you choose reserved capacity later — batching and KV-cache behavior matters for long-context cases.
[01:50] Nina: Can you explain what you mean by golden prompts? Is that like a seed set?
[02:10] Olivia: Yeah, golden prompts are small set — maybe 8-12 canonical prompts — that represent critical product flows. These are manually curated by Cardinal and used for continuous regression checks. Example: a 2-sentence news article => 3-bullet summary; or support ticket => one-line action item.
[02:40] Maya: We can produce those. We'll pick 8 to start: 4 high-frequency happy paths, 4 edge/failure cases.
[03:05] Samir: For POC scope, we're proposing a 6-week pilot: 2 weeks ingest & prep, 2 weeks initial runs and tuning, 2 weeks regression and final validation. Does that align?
[03:30] Maya: Yes that timeline is fine.
[03:45] Olivia: On sample sizes — for a meaningful statistical signal we recommend at least 2k reference pairs for the main eval; stratify by length buckets: short (<50 tokens), medium (50-200), long (>200). Also include a small adversarial subset ~200 examples.
[04:10] Ethan: 2k is doable, we'll anonymize. Question: do you need human reference summaries or can we use existing product-generated ones?
[04:30] Olivia: Prefer human gold references for scoring. If you only have machine outputs we can still run relative regressions, but absolute quality thresholds need human references.
[04:50] Trevor: What about hallucination metrics? We have a lot of entity-heavy text where hallucinations are fatal.
[05:10] Olivia: Good — proposed approach: two-pronged. 1) Automated heuristics: named-entity overlap + fact-check flags (e.g., dates, numbers) to detect potential hallucinations; 2) Human spot-checks on a sampled slice. We'll report hallucination rate as percent of outputs with at least one factual error per 1000. Target for POC: <5% on representative sample, <2% on golden prompts.
[05:45] Maya: Sounds reasonable. How do you score formatting/structure compliance? We have strict JSON-like output for our API.
[06:05] Olivia: We'll add format checks: schema validation runs (JSON parse success, required keys present), plus a scoring penalty for structural issues. For the quality composite we use: composite_score = 0.6 * semantic_similarity + 0.3 * format_score - 0.1 * hallucination_penalty. Semantic similarity is measured by BERTScore / embedding cosine overlap to human reference, normalized 0-1.
[06:45] Diego: Note that BERTScore can favour verbosity; we'll cap length factors or use length-normalized ROUGE-L as cross-check.
[07:05] Samir: Right — practice is to use multiple signals: embedding sim, ROUGE-L, and exact-match for critical fields. We'll provide the harness to compute all three and a way to tune weights.
[07:30] Nina: For regression tests, how often will you run them and what's the automation path?
[07:50] Olivia: The plan: run the full eval suite on every model candidate snapshot. Golden prompts run in CI on every commit to the model serving branch — that should be quick. Full 2k batch runs nightly or on-demand; we'll give an estimated runtime.
[08:10] Ethan: Runtime estimate? If you spin up a small cluster how long will 2k items take?
[08:30] Olivia: Rough estimate on our hosted GPU profile: single instance with batch size 8 should run 2k items in ~2-3 hours depending on sequence length. We'll give exact perf numbers once you share length distribution.
[08:55] Trevor: We'll share a histogram in the next day.
[09:10] Samir: Back to scoring thresholds — what do you want as pass/fail for the POC?
[09:25] Maya: We want customer-facing quality comparable to our current system: hallucination under 5%, format success >98%, semantic sim (composite) >= 0.65. If we hit those with similar latency, we'd be comfortable moving to Dedicated for pilot.
[09:55] Olivia: We'll set those as proposed success criteria. If the initial candidate misses one metric but exceeds others, we'll do a root-cause and micro-tuning phase — that fits into the 2-week tuning slot.
[10:15] Diego: Also capture failure modes — e.g., hallucinations driven by out-of-distribution inputs — we'll annotate and add to regression set.
[10:35] Maya: On tooling, can we see diffs of outputs vs reference? We need human review flows.
[10:50] Olivia: Yes, our eval UI shows side-by-side diff, a confidence score, and an annotation panel for graders to tag hallucination types. We'll give you access to a demo tenant.
[11:10] Samir: For datasets, you mentioned adversarial subsets. Any guidance on composition?
[11:30] Olivia: Include items with unusual entity names, mixed-language segments, truncated context, and long documents where the model must compress relevant facts. Also synthetic perturbations where facts are modified. Around 200-300 examples.
[11:55] Trevor: On privacy, these samples will contain PII maybe. Can Redwood eval harness run in our VPC?
[12:15] Samir: For the POC we can run evaluation either on hosted or in your VPC if you prefer private runs. If you need on-prem, we have a private deployment option but that's a larger engagement. For now we can do S3-ingest to our secure eval runner with NDA in place.
[12:40] Maya: NDA is already signed; we prefer to keep data in our cloud region. We'll request VPC-eval later if we proceed to Dedicated.
[12:55] Olivia: On the scoring spreadsheet, we'll publish a template with computed fields: per-example metrics (ROUGE-L, BERTScore, embedding_cosine), format_ok boolean, hallucination_flag boolean, and overall composite score. We'll also output percentile summaries and confidence intervals.
[13:20] Nina: How do you compute confidence intervals? Bootstrap?
[13:35] Olivia: Yes bootstrap on the sample, 1k resamples to estimate 95% CI. We'll report margin-of-error for the composite score.
[13:50] Ethan: About golden prompts — we want them in product-like syntax, including system instructions. Can Redwood run system+user prompt combos?
[14:10] Olivia: Absolutely. The harness supports prompt templates including system role, tool calls, and function responses. We'll also record token counts for cost analysis.
[14:35] Samir: Speaking of cost, initial POC cost estimate depends on run frequency and model size. We'll provide a cost model with per-1000-token costs and an estimated total for the planned eval runs.
[14:50] Maya: Please include Dedicated vs hosted cost delta — that's an evaluation criterion for us.
[15:05] Samir: Will do.
[15:20] Diego: A technical caveat: when measuring semantic sim over long summaries, embeddings can saturate. We'll include chunked similarity measures too.
[15:40] Olivia: Good call. We'll add a long-doc pipeline: chunk->embed->aggregate similarity.
[15:55] Nina: What about regression detection thresholds? How do you handle noisy signal?
[16:10] Olivia: We'll use a combination: flagging when composite score drops more than X std deviations or absolute delta greater than Y points. We'll tune X/Y with you during early POC runs.
[16:30] Maya: Can you give an example of a fail-trigger?
[16:45] Olivia: Example: composite score drops by 0.05 absolute and hallucination rate increases by >1 percentage point on golden prompts — that's an automatic blocker to rollout. We'll define exact thresholds in the SOW.
[17:05] Ethan: For human eval, how many annotators per example?
[17:20] Olivia: For critical subsets we recommend 3-way overlap and majority vote; for the larger corpus 1-way with spot-checks. We'll provide annotation guidelines.
[17:40] Samir: Any legal/compliance asks?
[17:55] Maya: Make sure logs are masked and access-controlled; we need audit logs for graders.
[18:15] Diego: Redwood's console supports RBAC and audit trails; graders can be scoped to only see masked data.
[18:35] Trevor: Also SSO/SAML integration for our team.
[18:50] Samir: We support SAML. We'll include instructions.
[19:05] Nina: On edge-case tracking, we'd like a living spreadsheet that grows as we find new failure modes.
[19:20] Olivia: We'll link that as a shared doc in the eval repo.
[19:35] Maya: Ok, recap and next steps?
[19:50] Samir: Recap: 6-week POC, 2k gold references, 8 golden prompts, adversarial 200 samples, scoring rubric with composite formula, hallucination target <5%, format success >98%, composite >=0.65. Redwood to share harness, scoring template, cost estimate. Cardinal to upload data and confirm prompt list.
[20:15] Maya: I'll assign internally and we'll aim to upload by 2025-04-10.
[20:30] Olivia: We'll send the harness link by Friday 2025-04-04 and schedule a follow-up to walk through the template on 2025-04-11.
[20:45] Trevor: Thanks everyone.
[20:55] Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up via email and attach the SOW draft.
[21:05] End meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: Automated transcription had occasional mislabels (e.g., KV-cache -> KV-cash, KMS sometimes spelled K M S in transcript). There is some overlap talk between 00:10-00:30.
